import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 238

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/238](https://www.erdosproblems.com/238)
-/

open scoped Topology
open Set Filter Real

namespace Erdos238

/--
Let `c₁, c₂ > 0`. Is it true that for any sufficiently large `x`, there exists more than
`c₁ * log x` many consecutive primes `≤ x` such that the difference between any two is `> c₂`?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_238 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (c₁ > 0) (c₂ > 0), ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop, ∃ (k : ℕ),
    c₁ * log x < k ∧ ∃ f : Fin k → ℕ, ∃ m, (∀ i, f i ≤ x ∧ f i = (m + i.1).nth Nat.Prime)
    ∧ ∀ i : Fin (k - 1), c₂ < primeGap (m + i.1) := by
  sorry

/--
It is well-known that the conjecture above is true when `c₁` is sufficiently small.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_238.variants.small_c1 : ∀ c₂ > 0, ∀ᶠ c₁ in 𝓝[>] 0, ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop, ∃ (k : ℕ),
    c₁ * log x < k ∧ ∃ f : Fin k → ℕ, ∃ m, (∀ i, f i ≤ x ∧ f i = (m + i.1).nth Nat.Prime)
    ∧ ∀ i : Fin (k - 1), c₂ < primeGap (m + i.1) := by
  sorry


end Erdos238

reformulations.difference: The inferred type of c₂ is ℕ rather than an arbitrary positive real constant. Also, the statement checks the k−1 internal adjacent prime gaps rather than explicitly requiring separation between every pair of distinct primes.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Positive integer thresholds are cofinal among positive real thresholds: for any real C > 0, choose an integer N > C and use the assertion for N. Conversely, restrict the real-threshold assertion to positive integers and cast the inequalities. Nat.nth Nat.Prime is strictly increasing, so for i < j the difference between entries j and i is at least the adjacent gap following i. Thus adjacent separation implies all-pairs separation; the converse follows by taking adjacent pairs. Fin (k−1) indexes exactly the internal gaps of the k primes. The threshold equivalence and adjacent/pairwise equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

reformulations.difference: The variant likewise uses natural-number gap thresholds and adjacent gaps. It expresses sufficiently small positive c₁ using the filter 𝓝[>] 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same cofinal-threshold argument works with the nested eventual quantifiers: choose the integer threshold before choosing the small-c₁ neighborhood, preserving the permitted dependence on c₂. Adjacent separation is equivalent to pairwise separation as above. On ℝ, eventual truth in 𝓝[>] 0 is exactly ∃ δ > 0, ∀ c₁, 0 < c₁ → c₁ < δ → P c₁. These equivalences were proved in the scratch file. Erdős's 1949 Theorem 3 explicitly supplies a positive logarithmic block-length constant depending on the gap threshold, agreeing with this quantifier order.

review.notes: Both declarations were checked. Direct requests to erdosproblems.com/238 and its LaTeX endpoint returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive user agents; the mathematics was instead verified against the original 1955 paper and its cited 1949 theorem. The current public Erdős-problem database records #238 as open. Lean experiments confirmed the first prime gaps, strict prime enumeration, absence of intervening primes, nontriviality of both filters, and that fixed positive c₁ forces k > 1 eventually, excluding empty/singleton vacuity. The equivalence proofs compile and have no sorryAx dependency. All experiments are under /workspace/review/; no repository files were edited.
